fact_claims.verbatim: company-wide thermal incidents: 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a written incident report and available investigation findings within 10 calendar days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a model-specific hazard or a need to stop use, inspect, or repair a unit.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator review; a model may not be marketed only if the regulator determines, after review, that corrective measures are inadequate to address an unacceptable safety risk. Results must be provided in plain language to customers who buy or own that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be publicly disclosed.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off beginning 12 months after adoption. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers must provide a compatible shut-off upgrade or other regulator-approved equivalent within 72 months, where technically feasible; customers must be notified of any units that cannot be upgraded and the available risk-reduction measures.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and installation environment and validated through regulator-approved testing.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A verified model rate above 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year triggers regulator review and a mandatory recall unless the regulator determines, based on documented evidence, that an equally protective corrective action resolves the risk. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material model-specific hazards and provide instructions for inspection, repair, or stopping use.

document.section_notes: The final rules set a 24-hour incident-reporting duty for all thermal incidents, which is the strongest element and benefits both firms' unreported incidents. S2 drops any numeric sales limit: the 5% failure rate only triggers review and corrective action, with sales stopping only if the regulator later finds remediation inadequate, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 keeps an 8-per-100k recall trigger but allows open-ended corrective action instead of recall, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). Customer result disclosure is specified only as 'plain language' without an explicit numeric rate, so I coded it as pass/fail only; this is a judgement call.
